answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by narrowing entry to a single inlet: each newcomer must complete a sequential apprenticeship under one established mentor with only a few open slots. The apprentice builds a timber-solid record of verified, dependent tasks, each checked in public view before the next unlocks, while the mentor stakes standing on the apprentice's conduct. Every extra fake identity needs another scarce slot and another full sequence, so cost grows with each copy, and the resulting trust is a pearl earned slowly, never bought in bulk.
